I have worked this land for 45 years. I am 63 now, never went to school, but the land taught me everything I need. There are only two of us at home. My 12 mu in Quzhou County grows winter wheat and summer maize, same as every farm around here.

For wheat: Every October, after ploughing the field properly, I sow improved wheat seed I get from the township supply store. I spread compound fertilizer as the base, and when the wheat turns green in spring, I top-dress with urea. I have my well, so water is not my worry. I will irrigate four times: the winter water before the deep freeze, the green-up water, the heading water, and one more when the grain is filling. I spray twice — once for weeds, and once if aphids or rust show up. If the weather is fair, I will harvest about 550 kg per mu in early June.

For maize: The same day the wheat comes off, I plant hybrid maize directly into the wheat stubble without ploughing. The summer season is too short to waste days turning the soil. I put down fertilizer with the planter, and at the big trumpet stage I add more nitrogen. I irrigate three times: right after sowing if the soil is dry, when the stalks are growing fast, and when the tassels emerge. I spray three times — herbicide once, and twice for corn borers and armyworms. By late September I expect around 650 kg per mu.

I do it this way because this is what has fed my family for half my life. I trust my eyes and my hands more than anything written in a book.
